results.name: clean_rule_member_inside_minus_outside_hull
results.description: In >=2-example sets whose examples all belong to some narrow rule (<=25 members), yes rate for non-example members of the smallest such rule lying inside the examples' range minus those outside it; observed above null means people restrict a rule to the examples' magnitude range more than the model (range only via separate interval hypotheses), below means less.

results.name: parity_contrast_parity_only_sets
results.description: In >=3-example sets whose examples all share a parity but no narrow rule (<=25 members, not odd/even/contains-digit) covers them all, yes rate for same-parity non-example targets minus opposite-parity targets; observed below null means people generalise a bare parity rule less than the model's equal-prior odd/even hypotheses predict, above means more.

results.name: outlier_vs_clean_rule_member_yes
results.description: Yes rate for non-example members of the majority narrow rule in >=3-example sets with one outlier, minus yes rate for non-example members of the covering narrow rule in clean >=3-example sets; observed below null means one outlier undermines the rule more than the model's uncertain-reliability stray account predicts, above means people shrug off outliers more readily.

results.name: contains_digit_only_member_yes
results.description: In >=2-example sets whose examples all contain some digit d but no narrow rule covers them all, yes rate for non-example targets containing d that belong to no narrow rule containing >=2 examples; observed below null means people use 'contains digit d' concepts less than the model's equal rule prior grants them, above means more.

results.name: rulecount_outlier_excuse_contrast
results.description: In >=3-example sets where a narrow rule covers all examples but one, yes rate for non-example members of that rule when the outlier belongs to many of the model's rules (>=6) minus when it belongs to few (<6); observed below null means people do not excuse richly-associated outliers more than plain ones as much as the rule-count familiar-stray model predicts, above means even more.

results.name: outlier_set_inhull_nonmember_yes
results.description: In >=3-example sets where a narrow rule covers all examples but one, yes rate for non-example targets outside that rule lying within the range of the rule-following examples; observed above null means people fill in the magnitude range of noisy sets more than the model (which explains the outlier as a stray and favours the rule) predicts, below means less.

results.name: example_as_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate when the target is one of the shown examples; observed below null means people endorse the shown examples less than the model's posterior membership (which counts every example as in-concept unless written off as a stray), above means more.

results.name: final_digit_vs_arithmetic_rule_preference
results.description: In >=2-example sets covered both by an 'ends in d' rule and by an arithmetic narrow rule (multiples/powers/squares/cubes/primes), yes rate for non-example targets only in the final-digit rule minus targets only in the arithmetic rule(s); observed above null means people favour surface final-digit rules over arithmetic ones more than the model's equal prior plus size principle predicts, below means they favour arithmetic rules more.
